images.threadTitle: Build a portfolio someone can verify
images.alt: Show the failure case. Teaching example: withdrawal tests. Side-by-side comparison. Allowed caller; Transfer succeeds; Check the expected result; Rejected caller; Caller lacks permission; Check the rejection. Include setup steps, the test command and known limits.

images.threadTitle: Build a portfolio someone can verify
images.alt: Connect content to an action. Proposed wallet-tutorial funnel. An ordered teaching sequence. Tutorial reader; Audience for the guide; Setup attempt; User starts the task; Setup completion; User reaches the intended action. Record measurement limits. Impressions do not show setup completion.

images.threadTitle: Build a portfolio someone can verify
images.alt: Document a repeatable task. Sample support runbook. Paired rows link each subject to its action or condition. User; Sends an error report; Moderator; Assigns an owner and next update; Engineer; Investigates and records the resolution. Make the next handoff explicit.

images.threadTitle: Build a portfolio someone can verify
images.alt: Label the evidence honestly. Three evidence formats. Side-by-side comparison. Public work; Link the artifact; Name your contribution; Approved redaction; Explain the constraint; Show permitted material; Personal exercise; Label it as practice; Describe your decisions. Use the evidence status that matches the work.

images.threadTitle: Build a portfolio someone can verify
images.alt: Run the reviewer check. Before applying. A reusable checklist with empty checkboxes. Evidence link; Open it while logged out.; Relevant sample first; Make the role match visible.; Authorship clear; Name your contribution.; Limits stated; Explain one limitation. The reviewer should not need to request access.

images.threadTitle: Understand token approvals before signing
images.alt: Read the permission you are granting. ERC-20 approval. Educational relationship diagram. Token holder; Account granting permission; Approved spender; Address receiving permission; Token contract; Records the allowance for this token and spender on this network. Check token, spender, amount and network before approving.

images.threadTitle: Understand token approvals before signing
images.alt: Compare the trade and the cap. Hypothetical token-quantity example. Two proportional bars: the 200-token cap is ten times the 20-token trade. Planned trade; 20 tokens; Requested cap; 200; Review the difference.; Where supported, set a cap for the intended use. The requested allowance is larger than the planned trade.

images.threadTitle: Understand token approvals before signing
images.alt: Disconnecting and revoking differ. Two separate states. Side-by-side comparison. Disconnect website; Changes the site connection; Onchain allowance remains; Revoke allowance; Submit on the relevant network; Check confirmation; fee normally applies. Only the revocation changes the spending permission.

images.threadTitle: Understand token approvals before signing
images.alt: A signature can carry spending authority. ERC-2612 permit. An ordered teaching sequence. Read the permit; Spender, amount and submission deadline; Sign the approval; No gas paid at this signing step; Later onchain submission; Someone can submit the signed permit. The deadline limits submission, not the resulting allowance lifetime.

images.threadTitle: Understand token approvals before signing
images.alt: Check the NFT permission scope. NFT operator permissions. One highlighted NFT is contrasted with all NFTs in the same collection contract. One-item approval; A; B; C; One approved NFT; Collection-wide; A; B; C; Every NFT you own from this collection contract; Check the named operator. Collection-wide means one collection contract, not every NFT in a wallet.

images.threadTitle: Understand token approvals before signing
images.alt: Keep an allowance review record. Allowance review inventory. A worksheet with explicitly labeled blank personal fields. Account and network; [scope to review]; Spender; [approved spender]; Remaining allowance; [current permission]; Revocation receipt; [confirmed transaction]. Revocation cannot reverse a transfer or repair an exposed private key.

Security interviews

Credit what the contract receives

Answer

Transfer fees and rebases. For supported fee-on-transfer tokens, credit the received balance delta. Rebases need separate accounting or explicit rejection.

The balance-delta pattern assumes compatible token behavior and safe call handling; it is not universal support for arbitrary tokens.

images.alt: Interview question AUD-I-02 on signature replay, with four checks: valid signer, intended domain, unused nonce and unexpired deadline. Bind the domain to chainId and verifyingContract and consume the nonce. A deadline limits time; EIP-712 alone does not prevent reuse.

images.renderedText:
Security interviews

Validity, domain, nonce, deadline

Answer

Reusing a valid signed action. Sign and consume a nonce, bind the domain to chainId and verifyingContract, and enforce a deadline. EIP-712 alone does not prevent reuse.

Fuzzing a custody vault

Answer

Generated inputs test properties. Echidna fuzzes call sequences; Foundry supports fuzz and invariant tests. Example for a simple custody vault: assets must cover recorded liabilities.

Passing a finite campaign is not proof of correctness; results depend on the property, harness, inputs and explored state.

images.alt: Interview question AUD-E-02 asks how unbounded loops in view functions can cause denial of service. Answer: eth_call uses RPC node resources and can hit gas caps or timeouts. A growing getAllOwners() can fail; bounded pages limit each read.

A free read still has execution limits

eth_call executes on an RPC node and can hit gas caps or timeouts. A getAllOwners() that grows forever can fail. Return bounded pages instead.
